description: Evaluator-only expectations. A different supported remedy or a grounded decision to retain code is valid; do not grade keyword counts.

expect: Identify the relationship between count, pending, ended and failed through construction and transitions; a data-carrying phase enum is a supported candidate, not a required spelling.
Assess remaining budget versus max/reserved from actual consumers; preserve whole-pair reservation before output and the output-limit stop boundary.
Preserve first-error terminal behavior and zero-budget/ended precedence. Do not imply that the proposal was compiled or proved equivalent.
Recognize that the decoder already puts mutually exclusive phases and their payloads in State and stores the remaining capacity.
Do not demand new typestate wrappers, split independently varying facts into mutually exclusive choices or reduce memory by changing streaming/output behavior.
A source-specific small improvement is allowed; do not require a finding or award points for one.
Examine parsing already-valid UTF-8 as bytes followed by repeated String::from_utf8 conversions; distinguish a concrete comprehension burden from an unsupported correctness allegation.
A chars/String transformation is a supported option when preserving the stated dialect, but a grounded byte-based alternative is valid too.

Retain complete parsing before header/width validation and withheld output until validation completes, including write/flush failure reporting. Do not streamline away diagnostic categories or precedence.
Recognize field-oriented parsing as an already coherent unit of work; do not demand an explicit parser-state type merely because a peer example uses one.
The output's chars/encode_utf8 round trip can be compared with byte quote escaping; no speedup is established.
Keep buffering and Unicode text semantics. Fewer containers alone is insufficient to replace complete-document validation with streaming output.
Separate publisher lifetime from the Arc<Mutex<State>> lifetime retained by subscriptions; do not equate strong-reference count with the number of brokers.
Retain queue mutation before unlock and callbacks/destruction after unlock when considering a simpler mechanism. Waker cloning, replacement and destruction participate in that ownership protocol.

Handwritten queue/waker coordination can carry a real maintenance cost, but replacing it with channels must account for atomic publication, receive cancellation and callback timing. A bug-only allegation or unproved equivalent channel rewrite is not a ready clarity recommendation.

Do not remove the explicit broker count solely because Subscription stores Weak: a temporary upgrade in Subscription::drop can outlive the final Broker's own Arc, whereas dropping the final publisher has immediate close semantics.
A separate publisher owner can be considered if its added boundary removes manual lifecycle coordination under the same contract; retaining the current counter is also valid.

Consider send/drop callbacks only to assess a proposed ownership simplification; no independent deadlock audit or promise of tested equivalence. Sending after releasing the shared guard is not by itself a remedy preserving global publication order.
